title: Sylow subgroup counts and normality
terms: Sylow subgroup; Sylow conjugacy theorem; Sylow counting theorem.

If |G| = p m with p prime and p ∤ m, a Sylow p-subgroup has order p . Sylow’s theorems assert
existence, conjugacy of all such subgroups, and that their number n divides m and satisfies

Combine congruence and divisibility before doing detailed group calculations. Distinct sub-
groups of prime order intersect only at the identity, enabling element counts. The analogous

claim for subgroups of order p with a > 1 is false; their intersections can be nontrivial. Unique-
ness of one Sylow subgroup does not automatically make the whole group abelian.

question.text:
Every group of order 45 has how many Sylow 5-subgroups?
(A) 1
(B) 3
(C) 5
(D) 9
(E) The number cannot be determined.

solution.text:
The number divides 9 and is congruent to 1 modulo 5. Among the divisors 1, 3, 9, only 1
satisfies the congruence. Thus this subgroup is unique and normal.

question.text:
For a group G of order 30, which assertion must hold?
(A) G is cyclic.
(B) G has a normal Sylow 2-subgroup.
(C) At least one of its Sylow 3- and Sylow 5-subgroups is normal.
(D) Every Sylow subgroup is normal.
(E) G has an element of order 30.

solution.text:
Sylow gives n ∈ {1, 6} and n ∈ {1, 10}. If both exceeded 1, the distinct prime-order sub-
5 3
groups would contribute 6(5 − 1) + 10(3 − 1) = 44 nonidentity elements, more than 29. Thus
one count is 1. The dihedral group of order 30 refutes the stronger alternatives.

A group of order 72 has a unique Sylow 3-subgroup. How many elements g satisfy g = e?
(A) 1 (B) 3 (C) 8 (D) 9 (E) 24

solution.text:
9
If g = e, its order divides nine, so the cyclic subgroup it generates is a 3-subgroup and is
contained in the unique Sylow 3-subgroup P . Conversely, |P| = 9, so every element of P
9
satisfies g = e by Lagrange. Exactly its nine elements qualify, whether P is cyclic or not.

question.text:
If P and Q are distinct Sylow 2-subgroups of S , what is |P ∩ Q|?
4
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 8

solution.text:
The Klein four-group V = {e,(12)(34), (13)(24), (14)(23)} is normal in S . For any Sylow
4
2-subgroup P , the product PV is a subgroup of power-of-two order containing P; its order
cannot exceed eight, the largest power of two dividing 24. Hence V ⊆ P , and likewise
V ⊆ Q. Their intersection has order at least four and divides eight. Order eight would give
P = Q, so it is four.

question.text:
If a finite group has exactly one Sylow p-subgroup P , what must hold?
(A) G is abelian.
(B) Every element of G has order a power of p.
(C) P is contained in the center.
(D) P is cyclic.
(E) P is normal.

solution.text:
Conjugating a Sylow p-subgroup gives another Sylow p-subgroup. Uniqueness therefore
makes every conjugate equal to P, which is normality. The subgroup need not be cyclic or
central.
